agent_report.summary:
Merged PR #45 (Issue #44 — completed priorities and tasks sink to the bottom, plus a large-day usability check). CI was green, Codex reported no issues, and the published evidence artifact confirmed the sink, the seeded 40-task day at 360/1280px and the required screenshots. Two things I recorded in the PR review: Issue #44's own text was self-contradictory (it called the within-completed-group order 'insertion order' while its worked example required the reverse) and the worker correctly implemented the worked example; and the PR fixed a pre-existing bug beyond the Issue's letter, where every writer built its next state from the getDay view and stored it back, baking time-sorted commitments into storage — split into rawDay for writers and getDay for readers.

With work in flight at zero, I opened Issue #46, a visual-identity pass, and labelled it ready. Every capability GOAL.md names is now implemented and tested; the only Definition of Done item with no dedicated work behind it is the visual-quality expectation. Two concrete defects ground the Issue: six panels carry six different top-border styles (solid, dashed, double, dotted) that distinguish nothing a reader needs, and there is no typeface decision at all. Scope is one coherent accent system, a self-hosted open-licensed font with an offline-survival test, a type scale from :root tokens, and a contrast check — no behaviour, layout or copy changes, with an explicit fallback path if no font file can be fetched in the runner.

The project is not DONE: the visual-quality item is unmet and #46 is open. No blocked, human or new request Issues needed handling.
